rounds.proof_sketch: The mutation changes '3' to '4' inside the comment text '// Step 3: Compute final log_softmax values' -> '// Step 4: Compute final log_softmax values'. Comments are stripped during C/C++/CUDA preprocessing and generate zero machine code. The compiled kernel binary is byte-for-byte identical between original and mutant.
rounds.survival_reason: This mutation only modifies text inside a C++ comment on line 91. The const_perturb mutation operator incorrectly identified the literal '3' within the comment string '// Step 3:' as a mutable numeric constant. Comments have no semantic effect in C/C++/CUDA - they are completely removed during preprocessing before compilation. The actual computation (finding max, computing sum of exponentials, and outputting val - log_sum_exp) is completely unchanged. Both versions compile to identical CUDA PTX/SASS instructions. This explains why Layer 2 testing showed bitwise identical outputs across 112+ diverse test rounds - the kernels are genuinely the same.
rounds.kill_strategy: This mutant is truly unkillable because the mutation affects only a comment string, not executable code. No input values, shapes, dtypes, or configurations can cause a comment to influence computation. The mutation tool has a false positive - it detected a numeric literal '3' inside comment text and treated it as a mutable constant.
rounds.recommendations: Mutation testing frameworks should exclude string literals inside comments from constant perturbation. A preprocessing step that strips comments before AST analysis would prevent these false-positive 'equivalent mutants' from consuming test resources.
